title: Nested calls expose identities but not runtime frames

minimal_reproducer.observation: wrapper calls increment; runtime trace contains increment operation identities but no call/return frame events

expected_semantics: An execution event inside a nested function should identify the active frame, parent frame, captures, and call/return ancestry.
actual_behavior_limitation: The execution envelope is for the requested wrapper and raw entries have block/operation identity only. The debugger can derive one entry frame and cannot claim a nested call stack.
why_capability_matters: Failure analysis and backtraces require knowing which function invocation owned a state transition, especially for recursion, closures, and repeated calls.
current_workaround: Preserve all exact operation identities and static function identities; set frame availability to requested_entry_only and causal completeness to partial.

host_language_code_required.classification: temporary adapter caused by an identified MNCS pressure
host_language_code_required.why: Host code creates a transparent outer frame projection and no invented inner frames.

proposed_primitive_or_semantic_direction: Expose stable execution/frame/task identities and parent-child call transitions in a bounded runtime event stream, including closure capture references where applicable.
alternatives_considered: flatten all calls into one synthetic frame
resolution_criteria: A nested-call fixture returns exact frame-enter/frame-exit/call relationships and `inspect` can produce a truthful backtrace with no text inference.

campaign_review.disposition: Static nested-call correspondence is verified, but it is not a runtime frame/task ancestry contract.
campaign_review.workaround: Expose ordered block events and function identities as partial correspondence only.
